title: Robustness of the Page-Wootters construction across different pictures, states of the universe and system-clock interactions
version: arXiv:2204.11740v3 [quant-ph], 11 Sep 2023 (v1 25 Apr 2022, v2 27 Jun 2023); journal DOI 10.1103/PhysRevD.108.063507 (Phys. Rev. D 108, 063507, per arXiv metadata and Crossref). Read: arXiv v3 HTML, all of Secs. I-VII and Apps. A-B.
locators: Sec. II.1 assumptions 1-3, Eqs. (1)-(6) and footnote 3 (physical scalar product); Sec. II.2 Eqs. (7)-(9), footnote 4; Sec. III.1 Eqs. (10)-(22), footnote 7 (projective time measurements only); Sec. III.2 Eqs. (23)-(31); Sec. IV Eqs. (32)-(45), footnote 15; Sec. V.1 Eqs. (46)-(53) (interaction restrictions); Sec. V.2 Eqs. (54)-(68); Sec. V.3 Eqs. (69)-(73), footnotes 21-22; Sec. V.4 Eqs. (74)-(76); Sec. VI.1-VI.4 Eqs. (77)-(93); Sec. VII; Apps. A.1-A.3, B.1-B.2.
assumptions: Tensor split H_U = H_S (x) H_C; ideal clock with [t,h]=i, continuous non-degenerate t spectrum (footnote 15) except an uncoupled qubit-clock example (Sec. VI.2); projective time measurements only (footnote 7). Universe in an eigenstate of the total Hamiltonian with any eigenvalue E, or a mixed state commuting with it (Eq. 7). Interaction V restricted by Eq. (47) [H (x) 1 + 1 (x) h, V] = 0, Eq. (48) [1 (x) h, V] = 0, Eq. (50) at most linear in h; hence Eq. (51) V = X (x) h with [X,H]=0. 'Heisenberg picture' means a formal unitary change of basis U = exp(-i H (x) t) (Eq. 11) on the kinematical space, not the trinity's quantum symmetry reduction.
conclusion: Author's claims: PW construction can be reformulated in a Heisenberg picture by a formal unitary (Eqs. 11-22), unique up to local unitaries (App. A); entanglement not necessary for mixed universe states without interaction; with V = f(H) (x) h, each total-energy eigensector gives a self-adjoint effective Hamiltonian H_eff(E) = -g_E(H) (Eqs. 58, 66); a mixture over sectors gives non-unitary but CPTP system evolution (Eq. 70, footnote 21); unitarity only within a single eigensector; qubit examples show time-direction inversion for strong coupling (Sec. VI.3-VI.4).
proof_status: Derivations read; elementary and mostly explicit. Not independently reproduced except the two-sector mixed-state map of Eq. (90), whose non-monotone trace distance we checked (knowledge/clock-interactions/rijavec_backflow_check.py; our consequence, not the author's claim).
dependencies: Singh-Friedrich 2304.01263 for V proportional to H (x) h
open_questions: Author leaves open interactions for which t is not invariant under the picture change (Sec. VII, last paragraph), i.e. the [V,h] != 0 regime that RC-1 needs.
Does the two-sector non-unitary map survive when the universe state is restricted to a single constraint surface H = 0? Per Eq. (58), no: it is unitary there.
relevance: RC-1 neighbour. Treats clock-system interactions only in the class [V,h]=0 and [V,H]=0, the opposite of RC-1's [H_int,H_C] != 0. Bears on RC-5: a commuting interaction plus a stationary mixture over several total-energy eigenvalues already yields a non-unitary conditioned family with trace-distance revival (our derivation from Eq. 90).
limits: Ideal continuous clock, projective clock readings, one restricted interaction class; no Dirac-observable or relational-Heisenberg (symmetry reduction) comparison. Mixed universe states span several eigenvalues of the total Hamiltonian, so they are not states on a single constraint surface H=0. Single-author preprint later published; correctness of every step not audited.

title: Non-linear equation of motion for Page-Wootters mechanism with interaction and quasi-ideal clocks
version: arXiv:2107.11452v1 [quant-ph], 23 Jul 2021; only version on arXiv as of 2026-10-20; no journal reference on the arXiv page. Read: arXiv v1 HTML, all sections and Apps. A-D.
locators: Sec. II Eqs. (1)-(6); Sec. III Eqs. (7)-(13); Sec. IV Eqs. (14)-(17); Sec. V Lemma 1 Eqs. (18)-(19), Eqs. (20)-(35); Sec. VI; App. A Eqs. (36)-(39); App. B Eqs. (40)-(42); App. C Eqs. (43)-(50); App. D Eqs. (51)-(54).
assumptions: Finite d-dimensional quasi-ideal clock (Gaussian superposition of Salecker-Wigner-Peres time states on a Z_d time basis, Eq. 12), approximately covariant with error exponentially small in d (Eqs. 13, 18-19); interaction H_I = -G H_S (x) H_C (Eq. 20), which commutes with H_C; PW conditioning on the QIC state without stated physical inner product; global state built in App. A from an expansion using the SWP clock; perturbative in G and in the clock error; short-time truncation (Eqs. 30, 33).
conclusion: Authors' claims: with negligible clock error the conditioned dynamics is unitary with dilated Hamiltonian H_d = (T/d) H_S (1 + G H_S) (Eq. 25); including the QIC error, the mixed-state equation (Eq. 33) has decoherence-like and rho_S(0)-dependent terms, called non-linear, whose size shrinks with clock dimension.
proof_status: Derivation read; heuristic and perturbative, error terms bounded only for the clock evolution (Lemma 1). Not reproduced. Our reading: the rho_S(0) dependence enters through the definition of V (Eq. 52), which contains the conditioned state itself, while the conditioning of Eq. (15) is linear in the global state; whether the induced map rho_S(0) -> rho_S(tau) is non-linear is therefore not shown by the derivation.
open_questions: Is the claimed non-linearity a property of the map or of the chosen representation of the error term?
No Dirac or relational-Heisenberg counterpart is given.
relevance: Nearest finite-dimensional, non-ideal, interacting PW predecessor. Its interaction commutes with H_C and its clock POVM is only approximately covariant, so it does not cover RC-1's [H_int,H_C] != 0 case. Bears on RC-5 as a claimed clock-error source of non-unitary, initial-state-dependent conditioned dynamics.
limits: Single version preprint; perturbative and approximate; PW picture only; one interaction (gravitational-type, commuting with H_C). Another unaccepted lane (kb-pw-critiques worktree) holds an abstract-level record of the same paper under id pw-mendes-nonlinear-pw-2021; the coordinator should merge the ids.

title: The Perspectives of Non-Ideal Quantum Reference Frames
version: arXiv:2512.19343v2 [quant-ph], 22 Jun 2026 (v1 22 Dec 2025); no journal reference or DOI on the arXiv page as of 2026-10-20. Read: v2 HTML main text Secs. I-VI in full and App. I (comparison with perspective-neutral, operational and perspectival frameworks) in full; App. F opening (Abelian representation theory) read; Apps. B-E, G, H and the proofs in C-F located by keyword search only, not read.
locators: Abstract; Sec. II footnote 2 (G finite-dimensional unimodular Lie group, discrete groups included), Eq. (1) covariance, Eqs. (2)-(3) relationalization map, Theorem 1 Eqs. (7)-(10); Sec. III trivial and regular QRFs Eqs. (13)-(14); Sec. IV Eqs. (25)-(30); Sec. V Eqs. (31)-(40), Example 5 and the periodic-clock paragraph after Eq. (38); Sec. VI; App. I Proposition 16 Eqs. (75)-(80).
assumptions: Kinematical QRF framework: systems A and S with a global product representation U_A (x) U_S of a symmetry group G (Sec. II), covariant orientation POVM (Eq. 1), external (possibly fictitious) laboratory frame, incoherent group averaging (G-twirl). Theorem 1 proved rigorously for finite dimensions and compact G (Sec. II, App. C). Explicit perspectives for Abelian G with rank-one POVMs (Sec. V, App. F). No Hamiltonian constraint with interaction and no dynamics is derived.
conclusion: Authors' claims: every QRF has a perspective satisfying their perspective and invariance principles (Theorem 1); non-ideal QRFs make the described system superselected, the relationalization map fails to be an algebra homomorphism (Eq. 25), and the algebra generated by relational operators can exceed the relational operators (Eq. 26), interpreted as back-reaction on the frame; restricting to the trivial-representation sector reproduces perspective-neutral reduction maps (Proposition 16).
proof_status: Main-text theorem statements and examples read; the appendix proofs were not read or checked.
open_questions: Authors: 'It is interesting future work to study more concretely when these phenomena occur and what their dynamical causes are.' (Sec. VI).
How the superselection structure of a non-ideal Z_N clock perspective interacts with a coupling not commuting with the clock generator is not addressed.
relevance: Supplies the kinematics of non-ideal (including finite Abelian, so Z_N) reference-frame perspectives: superselection and non-homomorphic relationalization. Does not treat clock-system interaction or relational dynamics, so it does not settle RC-1.
limits: Kinematic only; global action is a product representation, which excludes interacting constraints; the only dynamical remark (Sec. V, periodic clock 'behaves as if A were an ideal clock' in low-energy sectors) is qualitative, without equations. Preprint; proofs unread.

title: Relational Dynamics with Periodic Clocks
version: arXiv:2409.06479v3 [quant-ph], 11 Mar 2026 (v1 10 Sep 2024); journal DOI 10.1088/1367-2630/ae46d0 (New J. Phys. 28, 034504 (2026), per Crossref).
locators: Abstract (claims 1-4); Sec. II.2 (no-interaction assumption, Eq. 2); Sec. III Example 6 (two-level clock) and footnote 11; Sec. IV.2 Example 10. Only these passages were read, located by keyword search in the v3 HTML.
relevance: The trinity for periodic clocks, the reference the 1912.00033 conclusion defers to. Per its abstract it establishes the Dirac / Page-Wootters / relational-Heisenberg equivalence relative to periodic clocks, and Example 6 shows finite-dimensional, non-ideal U(1)-covariant clocks are in scope. Sec. II.2 states: 'we shall henceforth assume that no interactions between C and S are present.' It therefore covers the uncoupled finite periodic non-ideal baseline of RC-1 but not the interacting case.
limits: Abstract plus four located passages only; theorems, proofs and the Z_N-versus-U(1) question (discrete readings) unread. Read in full before any RC-1 claim contract.

title: Quantum time and the time-dilation induced interaction transfer mechanism
relevance: Cited in 2409.06479v3 (footnote 11) as using qubit-clock coherent states 'for implementing a finite-dimensional analogue of the quantum time-dilation mechanism in the presence of gravitation-like interactions'. A finite-dimensional interacting PW lead for RC-1. arXiv preprint 2407.00161 per arXiv listing (title matched on 2026-10-20).
limits: Discovery only: title and Crossref metadata (Cafasso, Pranzini, Malo, Giovannetti, Chiofalo; Phys. Rev. D 110, 106014, 2024). Interaction class, clock covariance and pictures unknown. Must be read before RC-1 is called unaddressed.

title: Emergence of Gravitational Potential and Time Dilation from Non-interacting Systems Coupled to a Global Quantum Clock
relevance: Rijavec's ref. [31] for the gravitational-type coupling V proportional to H (x) h in PW. Abstract: couples mass-energy with coordinate time through a Wheeler-DeWitt-like constraint. Interaction class appears to be of the commuting H (x) h type (to be confirmed).
limits: Abstract only (v2, 16 Oct 2025; v1 3 Apr 2023). No journal reference on arXiv page. Interaction class, clock and pictures unverified.
